title: NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index (September 2026) — builder confidence, 10:00 a.m. ET, on the September FOMC decision day
source: IR: the publisher's own forward calendar — nahb.org/news-and-economics/housing-economics/indices/nahb-wells-fargo-housing-market-index-release-dates fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 47,131 bytes), whose "2026 HMI Schedule" table carries the standing note "Normal release time: 10:00 AM Eastern Time" and the row "Sept. 2026 | September 16, 2026". NAHB produces this series rather than aggregating it, so this promotes on the precedent nahb-hmi-2026-11-17 set from the same table one day earlier, and existing-home-sales-2026-11-12 (NAR's own calendar) before that. Corroborated twice more this session, both primaries: NAHB's live HMI page /indices/housing-market-index (HTTP 200, 61,528 bytes) reports "HMI Key Findings: August 2026" — the index up one point to 35, current sales 39, six-month expectations 43, buyer traffic 23, 35% of builders cutting prices at an average 6% — i.e. the edition its own schedule dates 2026-08-17, so schedule and output agree; and seven Wayback snapshots of the same schedule page (20200927, 20211021, 20220928, 20230906, 20240909, 20250821, 20260105) re-parse to 84 publisher-authored dates for 2020-2026, a maintained forward calendar rather than a one-off announcement. The FOMC collision is separately primary: federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm (HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes) lists "September 15-16*" for 2026 with the asterisk its own key defines as "Meeting associated with a Summary of Economic Projections". A scheduled date is NAHB's commitment and not a promise the tape is open — 2 of 80 elapsed rows (2023-06-19, 2024-06-19) fell on Juneteenth. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: The sixth time in seven years the HMI has landed on an FOMC decision day, and the sixth consecutive time that decision has been a dot-plot meeting — which this session shows is not a coincidence but the only way the collision can happen. Across 63 scheduled FOMC decision days 2020-2027 parsed from the Fed's own calendars, SEP meetings occupy day-of-month 8-22 (19 of 31 inside 15-20) while non-SEP meetings occupy day-of-month 1-7 and 26-31 — ZERO inside 15-20. All 84 publisher-authored HMI dates fall on day-of-month 15-20. The two calendars therefore intersect only on the quarterly SEP/dot-plot Wednesday, and every one of the five elapsed collisions (2020-09-16, 2020-12-16, 2021-12-15, 2022-03-16, 2022-06-15) is an SEP meeting. That matters because the FOMC day is loud in exactly the window the HMI's 10:00 release would have to occupy: on 52 in-window decision days ITB's open->close median is 1.5570% against a 0.9522% clean baseline (p=0.0011), XHB 1.4926% vs 0.8569% (p=0.0004), SPY 0.7130% vs 0.4658% (p=0.0058), ITB session range 2.9747% vs 2.0761% (p<0.0001) — while the overnight GAP narrows (ITB 0.3457% vs 0.5123%, p=0.0497; SPY 0.2047% vs 0.3339%, p=0.0290), so there is no quieter pre-open to read the print in either. Against that, the HMI's own contribution reproduces the sibling ledger's null on an independently re-derived date set: HMI-only ITB open->close 0.9514% vs 0.9522% (n=73, p=1.00). Nothing to attribute, and no power to attribute it with. `impact: low` and `symbols: []` are re-derived here, not inherited — no macro- or housing-keyed house playbook exists (docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md re-grepped 2026-09-06, 0 hits) and no instrument attaches. One correction to the sibling nahb-hmi-2026-11-17 entry, which recorded an "unbroken mid-month Monday/Tuesday convention": across the same 84 dates the split is Mon 27 / Tue 24 / Wed 20 / Thu 12 / Fri 1, so Mon+Tue is 51 of 84 (60.7%) and the 20 Wednesdays are precisely what makes an FOMC collision possible at all — 58 of 60 parsed FOMC decision days are Wednesdays. Two sibling lanes proposed this id independently on 2026-09-06 and both were read before this file was written: new-home-sales-2026-09-24 filed it on the FOMC-collision caution this session confirms and quantifies, and housing-starts-2026-09-17 filed it on the D-1 pairing, which holds here — 2026-09-16 -> 2026-09-17 is the September HMI -> New Residential Construction pair. Both proposals are now inert and stay where they are. Date `confirmed` on the publisher's own calendar; that licenses nothing, and the call is stand aside on every horizon.
